excerpt: === README.md (md) === # Colbumia 2020 2020 Computational Journalism Class === cheatsheets/Python_Cheatsheet.ipynb (notebook) === # Python Cheatsheet Welcome to our Python cheatsheet. We will be adding to this over the course of the semester. Feel free to add sections that you feel are helpful. There are other Python Cheatsheets that exist - here is a great one that we took inspiration from: [Python Crash Course](https://ehmatthes.github.io/pcc/cheatsheets/README.html) # Integers and Floating Point Numbers ```python # create a varible called hours and store the value 8 (an interger) hours = 8 # we can print out hours print(hours) # add 2 to hours hours = hours + 2 print(hours) # another way of adding 2 to the value stored in hours hours += 2 print(hours) # float (floating point numbers) price = 7.99 # add 1.00 to price price += 1.00 print(price) ``` ### Multiplication and Division ```python # multiplication print(10*3) # division print(8/2) # 3.3333333333333335 print(10/3) # "//" will discard the fractional leftovers print(10//3) ``` # Booleans ```python # we can store True or False in a variable mike_likes_loops = True mark_likes_loops = False mark_is_on_the_right_side_of_history = True # we'll see how to put these to use below ``` # Strings ```python # create two string variables first_name = "Mike" last_name = "Young" # we can print the strings print(first_name) print(last_name) # we can combine the two strings together ("concatinate") full_name = first_name + " " + last_name print(full_name) # get the "length" of a string (i.e. the number of characters) number_of_characters = len(first_name) print(number_of_characters) ``` ```python # if you want to put quotes inside a string # you can either "escape" the quotes by putting a "\" in front of each one full_name = "\"Young\" Mike Young" # or you could use single quotes on the outside full_name = '"Young" Mike Young' # and likewise if you wanted to use single quotes full_name = '\'Young\' Mike Young' # or: full_name = "'Young' Mike Young" # or even, the dreaded triple quotes (the backslash tells # Python that your command continues onto the next line) full_name_with_drama = \ """The "young", oh so young, Michael 'Mike' Young""" # note that we can put any quotes inside the triple # quotes and that when you print it, it keeps all of the # newlines you put in. This triple quote is good for # specifying documentation print(full_name_with_drama) ``` ### String Methods https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#string-methods ```python # "stripping" whitespace from the left and right hand side of a string is very helpful # let's create a string variable with a bunch of space on both sides and a "newline" at the end full_name_with_messy_whitespace = " Mike Young \n" # -> add print statements to see the output of these commands! <- # here, we can strip off the whitespace and # return a "cleaned up" version which we store in a new variable cleaned_up_full_name = full_name_with_messy_whitespace.strip() print(cleaned_up_full_name) # make it lower case lower_case_full_name = cleaned_up_full_name.lower() # make it upper case upper_case_full_name = cleaned_up_full_name.upper() ``` ```python # "splitting"
